subject: Is it possible to get an anisotropic Matérn model with INLA ?

messages.author: 06bb4192c46c7b61
messages.subject: Is it possible to get an anisotropic Matérn model with INLA ?
parts:
Hello everybody, 
I am wondering if the current version of R-INLA supports stationary spatial models inducing a Matérn covariance with a Mahalanobis distance instead of the Euclidean distance. 
Also, is it possible to do a nonstationary analyis like this without getting one's hands too dirty ?
Kind regards and as always congrats for all your wonderful work
Sébastien

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Is it possible to get an anisotropic Matérn model with INLA ?
parts:
Hi,

there's no simple support for this at the moment (but some people may
have ad hoc code for it).

One of my PhD students is working on it (and others may be as well) as
we've figured out how to parameterise the anisotropy in a better way.

For _known_ anisotropy, you can mimic it by transforming your
coordinates and mesh; by stretching the mesh in a certain direction
before using it, you'll reduce the correlation range in that direction
in the original space, etc.

You can also obtain the fem matrices for essentially the model from
Fuglstad et al via fm_fem(mesh, aniso=list(gamma=...,vec=...)), and
use those in a direct call to inla.spde.generic(), but that's very
manual, and also requires known anisotropy.

Finn
